Ibuprofen.label: Hypertension
Ibuprofen.detail: NSAIDs reduce antihypertensive efficacy and promote sodium/water retention, worsening blood pressure control

Ibuprofen.label: Heart failure
Ibuprofen.detail: NSAIDs cause fluid retention and reduce renal prostaglandin synthesis, precipitating acute heart failure decompensation

Ibuprofen.label: Active peptic ulcer / GI bleed
Ibuprofen.detail: NSAIDs directly damage the gastric mucosa and inhibit prostaglandin-mediated mucosal protection

Ibuprofen.label: Chronic kidney disease
Ibuprofen.detail: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandin synthesis, reducing GFR and accelerating CKD progression

Ibuprofen.label: Asthma / NSAID-sensitive respiratory disease
Ibuprofen.detail: NSAIDs trigger bronchospasm in aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease — affects ~10% of asthmatic patients

Ibuprofen.label: Atrial fibrillation / anticoagulation
Ibuprofen.detail: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk in patients already on anticoagulant therapy for AF

Aspirin.label: Gout / hyperuricemia
Aspirin.detail: Low-dose aspirin reduces renal urate excretion, raising serum uric acid and risking gout flares

Aspirin.label: Active peptic ulcer / GI bleed
Aspirin.detail: Aspirin directly damages the gastric mucosa even at low antiplatelet doses

Aspirin.label: Asthma / NSAID-sensitive respiratory disease
Aspirin.detail: Aspirin can trigger bronchospasm in aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease

Aspirin.label: Heart failure
Aspirin.detail: Aspirin at higher doses may worsen heart failure through prostaglandin inhibition; assess benefit vs. risk

Warfarin.label: Known bleeding disorder
Warfarin.detail: Anticoagulation is contraindicated in the presence of an active, uncontrolled bleeding disorder

Warfarin.label: Uncontrolled hypertension
Warfarin.detail: Severely uncontrolled blood pressure increases intracranial bleeding risk during anticoagulation

Warfarin.label: Hepatic disease
Warfarin.detail: Hepatic disease reduces synthesis of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, amplifying warfarin effect unpredictably

Warfarin.label: Recent intracranial event
Warfarin.detail: Recent intracranial haemorrhage is a relative contraindication; benefit-risk assessment required

Clopidogrel.label: Active GI bleed history
Clopidogrel.detail: Clopidogrel adds antiplatelet effect on top of an already compromised mucosal barrier

Clopidogrel.label: Known bleeding disorder
Clopidogrel.detail: Antiplatelet therapy is contraindicated in active, uncontrolled bleeding disorders

Metformin.label: Decompensated heart failure
Metformin.detail: Reduced cardiac output causes tissue hypoxia; metformin accumulation leads to lactic acidosis

Metformin.label: Significant hepatic impairment
Metformin.detail: Hepatic clearance of lactate is impaired, greatly raising lactic acidosis risk with metformin

Metformin.label: Iodinated contrast procedure
Metformin.detail: Withhold metformin 48h before and after iodinated contrast to prevent contrast-induced nephropathy + lactic acidosis

Carbamazepine.label: Bone marrow suppression / blood dyscrasia
Carbamazepine.detail: Carbamazepine can cause aplastic anaemia; contraindicated in pre-existing bone marrow depression

Carbamazepine.label: Hyponatraemia / SIADH
Carbamazepine.detail: Carbamazepine stimulates ADH release, worsening existing hyponatraemia

Carbamazepine.label: Hepatic disease
Carbamazepine.detail: Carbamazepine is hepatically metabolised; hepatic impairment raises drug and toxic metabolite exposure

Carbamazepine.label: Cardiac conduction disorder
Carbamazepine.detail: Carbamazepine can slow cardiac conduction; use with caution in pre-existing AV block

Oxcarbazepine.label: Hyponatraemia / SIADH
Oxcarbazepine.detail: Oxcarbazepine causes clinically significant hyponatraemia in ~2-3% of patients, higher risk if pre-existing

Oxcarbazepine.label: Hepatic disease
Oxcarbazepine.detail: Oxcarbazepine requires hepatic metabolism; monitor levels and tolerability in hepatic impairment

Phenytoin.label: Hepatic disease
Phenytoin.detail: Phenytoin is extensively hepatically metabolised; saturable kinetics mean small dose changes cause large level swings

Phenytoin.label: Depression
Phenytoin.detail: Phenytoin can exacerbate depressive symptoms; monitor mental health closely during treatment

Citalopram.label: Atrial fibrillation / QT disorder
Citalopram.detail: Citalopram causes dose-dependent QT prolongation; pre-existing AF or QT disorder raises arrhythmia risk

Citalopram.label: Bipolar disorder
Citalopram.detail: SSRIs can trigger manic episodes in bipolar disorder without adequate mood stabiliser cover

Citalopram.label: Epilepsy
Citalopram.detail: SSRIs can lower the seizure threshold at higher doses; monitor seizure frequency

Citalopram.label: Hepatic disease
Citalopram.detail: Citalopram clearance is reduced in hepatic impairment; use half the maximum dose

Escitalopram.label: Atrial fibrillation / QT disorder
Escitalopram.detail: Escitalopram causes dose-dependent QT prolongation; pre-existing AF or QT disorder raises arrhythmia risk

Escitalopram.label: Bipolar disorder
Escitalopram.detail: SSRIs can trigger manic episodes in bipolar disorder without adequate mood stabiliser cover

Escitalopram.label: Hepatic disease
Escitalopram.detail: Escitalopram clearance is reduced in hepatic impairment; use half the maximum dose

Amitriptyline.label: Cardiac conduction disorder / arrhythmia
Amitriptyline.detail: Tricyclic antidepressants block cardiac fast sodium channels; pre-existing conduction disease risks fatal arrhythmia

Amitriptyline.label: Angle-closure glaucoma
Amitriptyline.detail: Anticholinergic effect precipitates acute angle-closure glaucoma attacks

Amitriptyline.label: Hypertension
Amitriptyline.detail: Tricyclics can cause orthostatic hypotension and unpredictable BP changes, complicating hypertension management

Amitriptyline.label: Bipolar disorder
Amitriptyline.detail: Tricyclics can trigger manic switches in bipolar disorder

Amitriptyline.label: Epilepsy
Amitriptyline.detail: Tricyclics lower seizure threshold; use with caution and only if seizures are well-controlled

Atomoxetine.label: Hypertension
Atomoxetine.detail: Atomoxetine raises heart rate and blood pressure; pre-existing hypertension requires monitoring and may need antihypertensive adjustment

Atomoxetine.label: Cardiac arrhythmia
Atomoxetine.detail: Atomoxetine's sympathomimetic effect can worsen existing cardiac arrhythmias

Atomoxetine.label: Hepatic disease
Atomoxetine.detail: Atomoxetine is hepatically metabolised; hepatic impairment substantially raises drug exposure

Atomoxetine.label: Angle-closure glaucoma
Atomoxetine.detail: Mydriatic effect can trigger acute angle-closure episodes

Ondansetron.label: Atrial fibrillation / QT disorder
Ondansetron.detail: Ondansetron prolongs the QT interval; risk is higher in pre-existing QT disorders and with other QT-prolonging drugs

Ondansetron.label: Hypokalaemia
Ondansetron.detail: Ondansetron's QT-prolonging effect is amplified by electrolyte imbalance, particularly low potassium

Omeprazole.label: Osteoporosis
Omeprazole.detail: Long-term PPI use reduces gastric acid-dependent calcium absorption, worsening bone density

Omeprazole.label: Hypomagnesaemia
Omeprazole.detail: Long-term PPI use causes clinically significant hypomagnesaemia; can worsen pre-existing deficiency

Simvastatin.label: Hypothyroidism
Simvastatin.detail: Untreated hypothyroidism raises statin exposure and independently causes myopathy; treat thyroid disorder before or alongside statin initiation

Simvastatin.label: Active hepatic disease
Simvastatin.detail: Active hepatic disease or persistently elevated transaminases are contraindications for statin use

Simvastatin.label: Pre-existing myopathy
Simvastatin.detail: Pre-existing muscle disease substantially raises the risk of severe statin-induced myopathy

Atorvastatin.label: Hypothyroidism
Atorvastatin.detail: Untreated hypothyroidism raises statin exposure and independently causes myopathy; treat thyroid disorder before or alongside statin initiation

Atorvastatin.label: Active hepatic disease
Atorvastatin.detail: Active hepatic disease or persistently elevated transaminases are contraindications for statin use

Atorvastatin.label: Pre-existing myopathy
Atorvastatin.detail: Pre-existing muscle disease substantially raises the risk of severe statin-induced myopathy

Rosuvastatin.label: Active hepatic disease
Rosuvastatin.detail: Active hepatic disease or persistently elevated transaminases are contraindications for statin use

Rosuvastatin.label: Hypothyroidism
Rosuvastatin.detail: Untreated hypothyroidism raises myopathy risk with statins; address thyroid disorder first

Fluorouracil (5-FU).label: Cardiac disease
Fluorouracil (5-FU).detail: Fluorouracil causes cardiotoxicity (coronary vasospasm, arrhythmia) in ~7% of patients; pre-existing cardiac disease amplifies this risk

Capecitabine.label: Cardiac disease
Capecitabine.detail: Capecitabine (oral 5-FU prodrug) carries the same cardiotoxicity risk as 5-FU; use with caution in pre-existing cardiac disease

Capecitabine.label: Renal impairment
Capecitabine.detail: Capecitabine requires dose reduction in moderate renal impairment; contraindicated below eGFR 30

Irinotecan.label: Hepatic impairment / raised bilirubin
Irinotecan.detail: Irinotecan's active metabolite SN-38 is cleared hepatically; hepatic impairment raises SN-38 toxicity substantially

Irinotecan.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
Irinotecan.detail: Irinotecan diarrhoea is severe and life-threatening; pre-existing IBD dramatically worsens this risk

Azathioprine.label: Active infection
Azathioprine.detail: Azathioprine's immunosuppressive effect prevents adequate immune response to active infections

Azathioprine.label: Pre-existing malignancy
Azathioprine.detail: Long-term azathioprine use increases the risk of lymphoma and skin cancers; specialist risk-benefit assessment required

Tamoxifen.label: Thromboembolic history
Tamoxifen.detail: Tamoxifen increases the risk of DVT and pulmonary embolism; prior thromboembolism requires individual specialist risk-benefit assessment

Tamoxifen.label: Endometrial cancer history
Tamoxifen.detail: Tamoxifen has weak oestrogen-agonist effects on the endometrium; prior or current endometrial cancer is a relative contraindication

Amoxicillin.label: Glandular fever / EBV infection
Amoxicillin.detail: Amoxicillin causes a widespread maculopapular rash in >90% of patients with active EBV / glandular fever; it must be avoided

Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole.label: G6PD deficiency
Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole.detail: Sulfonamides cause haemolytic anaemia in G6PD-deficient patients

Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole.label: Folate deficiency
Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole.detail: Trimethoprim inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, worsening pre-existing folate deficiency and risking megaloblastic anaemia

Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole.label: Chronic kidney disease
Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole.detail: TMP-SMX raises serum creatinine and potassium; monitoring is essential in CKD

Abacavir.label: Cardiovascular disease
Abacavir.detail: Some studies associate abacavir with a modestly increased risk of myocardial infarction; warrants monitoring in high baseline CV risk

Allopurinol.label: Renal impairment
Allopurinol.detail: Allopurinol and its active metabolite oxypurinol are renally cleared; dose reduction is required to prevent toxic accumulation

Allopurinol.label: Acute gout flare
Allopurinol.detail: Starting allopurinol during an acute gout attack can prolong or worsen the flare; initiate during the inter-critical period instead

Codeine.label: Epilepsy
Codeine.detail: High-dose opioids can lower seizure threshold; monitor seizure frequency if codeine is used in epileptic patients

Codeine.label: COPD / respiratory failure
Codeine.detail: Opioids cause respiratory depression; pre-existing CO2 retention or respiratory failure is a near-absolute contraindication

Voriconazole.label: Hepatic disease
Voriconazole.detail: Voriconazole is hepatically metabolised and hepatotoxic; hepatic disease substantially raises liver adverse event risk

Levothyroxine.label: Atrial fibrillation
Levothyroxine.detail: Over-replacement with levothyroxine triggers or worsens AF; TSH must be monitored closely

Levothyroxine.label: Ischaemic heart disease
Levothyroxine.detail: Rapid correction of hypothyroidism increases myocardial oxygen demand; start at low dose and titrate slowly
